**Membership storage grows with watched pairs, not merely with users or videos.** A Bloom filter stores approximate membership compactly, allowing false positives but no false negatives for inserted items under ordinary operation. Its size depends on the number of retained user-video pairs and the chosen false-positive rate. [1](https://nlp.stanford.edu/IR-book/)

At a 1% target false-positive rate, the ideal formula gives about 9.6 bits per pair. Fifty decimal GB spread over 500 million users provides about 800 bits per user, enough for roughly 83 pairs per user before implementation overhead.

**That arithmetic rules out unrestricted lifetime history under the stated budget.** Choose a retention window, larger storage, tiered durable history, or a different error tolerance. False positives mean suppressing an unseen item, which may be acceptable only at a measured rate.

Standard Bloom filters do not support safe arbitrary deletion without additional structure. Count-Min Sketch estimates frequencies and tends to overestimate; it is not a drop-in exact history store. Define whether the product needs lifetime membership, recent exposure, or frequency before selecting the data structure.

**Technical details and references.**

The bound depends on the number of watched user–video pairs, not just the catalog size. For $n$ inserted pairs and false-positive probability $p$, a Bloom filter needs approximately $m=-n\ln p/(\ln2)^2$ bits and $k=(m/n)\ln2$ hashes. At $p=0.01$, this is about 9.6 bits per pair. [1](https://nlp.stanford.edu/IR-book/)

Fifty decimal GB provides about 800 bits per user for 500 million users, enough for only about 83 retained pairs per user at that error rate, before overhead. Thus unrestricted lifetime history cannot meet the stated limit. Choose a retention window, higher tolerated false positives, tiered durable history, or larger budget. Bloom false positives suppress unseen items; standard Bloom filters lack safe deletions. Count-Min Sketch estimates frequencies with overestimation and is not an exact substitute for arbitrary membership history.
